162.title: Strengthen evidence of deployed and model verifier equivalence

description: The logical route from the deployed verifier to the formal soundness endpoint, as it stands on main.

stages.title: Pin Lean to the deployed verifier
stages.claim: The Lean assembler and a captured Rust verifier MSM agree coefficient-for-coefficient, at a verifying key Lean derives rather than assumes.
stages.summary: The proof starts by fixing the object under study: the verifier's final multi-scalar multiplication. msmMatch_eval transfers a checked coefficient match to equality of group evaluations, and the statements of record now spell the verifying key as its end-to-end derivation from the ported configure/keygen rather than as the dumped record. The deployed evidence is still per-capture rather than a universal Rust-to-Lean equivalence, but the quantified random-evaluation match prices what a competing coefficient family would cost.
proves: The checked Lean and captured Rust MSM coefficients match, at the Lean-derived verifying key and the Lean-derived challenge schedule.
A matching MSM has the same group evaluation under any supplied URS.
A competing coefficient family that differs from Lean's anywhere agrees at a uniform point with probability at most (D + B)/p.
residuals: Rust capture provenance: the captured MSM, proof bytes, and oracle transcript are taken as faithful records of a deployed run.
Identifying the ported configure/synthesize with the deployed Rust circuit — the derivation is now in Lean, but its agreement with the shipped circuit is not.

stages.title: Turn acceptance into the IPA equation
stages.claim: An accepting assembled MSM yields halo2's explicit IPA verifier equation, with the generator term in closed fold form.
stages.summary: DeployedAccepts is the concrete MSM-equals-identity premise on the rejecting assemble?. deployedAccepts_verifierEq unfolds that compact check into the explicit equation, and deployed_gterm_foldAll rewrites its g-term as the closed-form generator fold the straight-line extractor reads. No forked-transcript compatibility lane is exported any more.
proves: The compact deployed accept implies the explicit verifier equation, with the verifier's rejection guards retained.
The deployed g-scalars fold exactly as the extractor's generator fold, so the equation is read at the extractor's own basis.
residuals: The empirical verifier-fingerprint boundary from the preceding stage.
Fiat-Shamir challenges still need a random-oracle interpretation before any probability is spent.

stages.title: Model the transcript and bound the adversary
stages.claim: The deployed squeeze schedule seals each challenge behind its own prefix, and a Q-query adversary's losses are an additive union of pinned root events.
stages.summary: Transcript-ordering lemmas seal each round prefix before its challenge, so every root set the argument prices is fixed before its squeeze. The adversary is a bounded-query adaptive query tree with eager whole-table semantics, and assembly provenance shows every point the multiopen MSM appends comes from the proof or the verifying key. Nothing here rewinds: the pinned-squeeze bounds replace the forking lemma the earlier development used.
proves: Round messages precede the challenges they must not influence, so each priced root set is pinned before its own squeeze.
A Q-query adversary's escape probability at one squeeze is bounded per point, and the events compose as an additive union rather than a joint coupling.
Ideal-oracle bounds transport to the deployed challenge conversion through an explicit statistical-distance premise (PMFEventBiasLE).
residuals: Blake2b and challenge decoding are idealized as a uniform random oracle; transcript injectivity is assumed.
The bound is over the modeled oracle table, not over the deployed hash's actual outputs.

stages.title: Classify one accepting execution
stages.claim: One accepting algebraic transcript is a clean IPA opening, an explicit relation over (g, U, W), or a squeeze-pinned bad-challenge event — with no rewinding.
stages.summary: The represented execution carries a coefficient vector for every group point the prover emits. straightLineIpaZeroOrRelation reads the symbolic IPA equation off that representation and returns the trichotomy as data; separateOrRelationWitness is the small kernel that compares two representations and returns their difference as relation coefficients when they disagree. PR #142 removed the recursive extractor, the transcript tree, and three-special-soundness from the live stack: nothing on this route re-runs the adversary.
proves: Every group point in the adversary's proof output carries its representation over the sampled augmented basis (g, U, W).
One accepting execution yields either the opening of the de-blinded commitment or explicit relation coefficients — never a merely existential claim.
The bad-challenge branch is a root event pinned before its squeeze, derived from the run's own query chronology rather than from the final proof value.
residuals: The representations are ghost extractor data: the result covers represented online-AGM adversaries, not arbitrary non-algebraic ones.
The relation branch is only a break under a computational assumption; the reduction to plain DL is priced two stages on.

stages.title: Recover the verifier's opened columns
stages.claim: The x4 collapse is a flat power batch, and Vandermonde inversion decodes it componentwise down to the individual queried member commitments.
stages.summary: deployedCommitment_x4_batch shows the deployed grouping itself has the flat power shape the decode inverts, so there is no separate 'flat model equals deployed' obligation. The live decode is the augmented opened-batch interface: the same inverse matrix decodes the witness vectors and their declared U- and W-components, and the x1 layer unbatches each point-set aggregate back to the member commitments. The batch is populated from explicit AGM coordinates, not from a rewind.
proves: The x4 decode consumes the deployed grouping's own aggregates, not modeled stand-ins.
The x1 unbatch pins the extracted witness to the actual queried member commitments, as an explicit two-level power combination.
The constraint layer reuses the run's own retained coordinates rather than choosing a fresh existential decode.
residuals: The decode avoids explicit root sets; those exclusions are priced with the challenge surfaces rather than assumed away.
Per-point claimed evaluations and the x-to-x3 quotient transport stay with the fingerprint half.

stages.title: Lift the point check to circuit satisfaction
stages.claim: Outside the Schwartz-Zippel bad set, the quotient point check implies the full combined gate, permutation, and lookup identity.
stages.summary: quotientCheck_sound bounds the roots of the constraint-difference polynomial, and the good challenge is derived from challenge uniformity rather than assumed: an accept event whose measure beats the budget contains an accepting challenge outside the bad set. The deployed fold combines the permutation and lookup constraint values too, and ConstraintRelations reads the copy-constraint equalities and the lookup inclusion back out of the satisfaction predicate.
proves: A good challenge turns the verifier's point identity into the full constraint polynomial identity.
Bad-set avoidance comes from an explicit probability budget, and the x-squeeze exclusion's pinning half is derived from the run's own query log.
Circuit satisfaction on the deployed path covers the gates, the permutation argument's copy constraints, and the lookup argument's inclusion.
residuals: hquot still carries the fingerprint-to-gate-check and x-to-x3 transport content on the compatibility rungs.
The grand-product telescoping and final lookup assembly are proven as structural results but their Schwartz-Zippel bridge is priced, not free.

stages.title: Price the relation branch
stages.claim: Every computed relation over (g, U, W) becomes either a plain discrete-log solution or one 1/|F| miss hyperplane.
stages.summary: The programmed-basis adapter plants the DL challenge in every basis slot as x·B + y·C with fresh pairs (Jaeger-Tessaro Lemma 3), rather than guessing which slot the relation will hit, so the loss is additive with no multiplicative factor. A nonzero challenge component yields the discrete log; a miss retains the exact relation with a proof that it annihilates the programming. The sampled-basis distribution equality is proven inside a uniform generator random-oracle model.
proves: A combined (g, U, W) equation whose coordinates disagree computes relation coefficients as data, not as an existential.
The programmed-basis conversion loses exactly one 1/|F| miss hyperplane per relation, with no augmented-basis cardinality factor.
Inside the generator random-oracle model, the reduction's sampled basis has the same distribution as the deployed setup.
residuals: Finite-security discrete-log hardness on Vesta is a caller-supplied premise; Lean asserts no generic-group DLOG success formula.
Identifying halo2's concrete hash-to-curve generator derivation with the uniform generator oracle is an out-of-Lean idealization, separate from the transcript random oracle.

stages.title: Let the adversary choose the statement
stages.claim: One online-AGM adversary returns the public inputs and proof together, and an executable extractor returns the private witnesses for every proof in the bundle or explicit relation coefficients.
stages.summary: The adaptive-statement game reconstructs the verifier transcript from the basis-dependent VK representation and the instance commitments derived from the adversary's own output, binding the selected instance prefix before theta. Its instance, pre-IPA, IPA, semantic, and source comparisons all consume one retained execution. The straight-line family is the fixed-statement sibling: both terminate in a data-bearing outcome, so neither existential relation availability nor a merely propositional statement branch counts as extracted knowledge.
proves: The adversary selects the public statement and the proof together, with the canonical verifying key and every selected instance commitment in the transcript prefix before theta.
The knowledge extractors are executable and return the actual private witnesses for every proof in the bundle, together with proofs that they satisfy the compiled Action specification.

The direct profiles separately account for random-oracle, group, and direct-coordinate work; the straight-line finder has a pointwise four-invocation bound, so no expectation or Markov tail enters the accounting.
residuals: The transcript representation of the verifying key is opaque: the game does not claim cross-key binding, which would need collision resistance of the concrete key hash.
Adversary PPT time and the concrete DLOG hardness bound remain external.

stages.title: Compose the opening, the circuit, and the budget
stages.claim: The extracted opening and the constraint identity form SnarkRelation, and the six advertised endpoints bound acceptance-with-extraction-failure at explicit resource ceilings.
stages.summary: SnarkRelation is the conjunction of one pinned IPA opening and circuit satisfaction for the same witness. Above it sit exactly six censused endpoints: two consensus-generic adaptive-statement Action bounds, three captured straight-line knowledge errors, and one consensus-maximum finite-security package. The adaptive-statement capstone bounds verifier acceptance when executable private-witness extraction fails by Adv_DLOG(2^126, 2^126) + 2^-83 at a 2^123 computational work target, for every consensus-valid bundle size.
proves: The opening and constraint branches refer to the same pinned verifier statement.
Every advertised endpoint is a top-level leaf named directly in a TrustBoundary census entry, so its own trusted base is checked rather than inherited.
The 2^-83 term is an independent statistical soundness error, and the endpoint requires no externally supplied traces, cuts, or views.
residuals: The endpoints keep named structural premises: B != 0 for the DLOG challenge point and injectivity of the basis query map, plus the static-check and x-squeeze-schedule interfaces on the straight-line rungs.
The recorded work factors are accounting scales the reduction was evaluated at, not proven end-to-end security levels.

stages.title: Stop at the exact formal boundary
stages.claim: The chain reaches executable witness extraction with explicit reduction disjunctions; it does not erase the remaining modeling and composition gaps.
stages.summary: The final view keeps hypotheses and out-of-Lean assumptions visible. The output-side floor has moved one step: Security.Ledger.Bridge.actionSpec_to_ledger now refines the Action circuit's postcondition to the games-facing ledger statement, so what is missing is the composition of the extracted bundle witness with that bridge, not the bridge itself. This is the honest endpoint: a large mechanized core with named inputs, probability budgets, and computational assumptions rather than an all-green claim.
proves: Every mechanized bridge shown in the map has a concrete Lean anchor on main.
The endpoint records reduction outcomes and residual premises without hiding them.
residuals: Composing the extracted ActionBundleWitness with the ledger bridge; Blake2b-as-RO, generator hash-to-curve-as-RO, the online-AGM idealization, finite-security DL hardness, and Rust-capture provenance.
Adversary running time, implementation work bounds, and the combined error budget across the whole protocol stack.
